Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
728 PM EDT Wed Sep 23 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Minor to moderate coastal flooding will continue around the 
Chesapeake Bay and tidal Potomac through Friday. Drier weather and 
breezy conditions return Thursday into the weekend despite a 
developing Nor'easter offshore. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Another damp and cool night ahead. Turning drier while 
remaining breezy Thursday and Friday.  

- 2) Remaining breezy while turning warmer this weekend despite 
uncertainty in regards to impacts from coastal Nor'easter nearby. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1... Another damp and cool night ahead. Turning drier 
while remaining breezy Thursday and Friday.  

Improving weather conditions tonight into Thursday as drier air 
filters in from the northeast. Some breaks were already visible
on satellite from northern VA points north and east as the 
drier air erodes the wedge. Strong 1040 mb high pressure over 
southeast Quebec will continue to wedge south through Thursday 
allowing for decreasing rain chances and cloud cover. At the 
same time, low pressure will begin to strengthen off the 
Delmarva/NC coast before riding north toward southern New 
England as a pretty impressive Nor'easter takes shape Friday 
into Saturday. 

For the remainder of the evening, expect pockets of drizzle and 
confined to locations west of the Blue Ridge and down into central 
VA. Elsewhere conditions will remain mostly dry with cloudy/mostly 
cloudy skies expected. Overnight lows tonight will fall into 
the upper 40s and mid 50s (mid 40s mountains). Winds will remain
elevated out of the northeast, with gusts to around 15-30 mph 
possible at times to the east of the Blue Ridge.

Drier weather returns Thursday and Friday although breezy conditions 
will remain as the upper level trough axis passes overhead. This 
will lead to more clouds than sunshine Thursday with better clearing 
Friday as more subsidence works into the region. Coastal low 
pressure will continue to deepen off the Delmarva coast leading to 
gusty north to northeast winds for both Thursday and Friday 
afternoon. Gale conditions will be likely across the open and middle 
waters as well as out along the Atlantic coast given the tightened 
pressure gradient. Gusts of 20-30 mph are expected with the highest 
likely along the waters and toward the ridges. Temperatures 
will stay below normal as a result, with highs in the 60s 
Thursday and upper 60s to near 70 on Friday.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Breezy and warmer this weekend, but forecast remains 
uncertain as Nor'easter impacts Northeast U.S. 

Anomalously strong surface ridge (by late September standards) 
finally weakens this weekend as a strong Nor'easter develops off the 
coast of Southern New England/LI. Ensemble members still show quite 
a bit of spread regarding the exact track of the Nor'easter. A few 
members show the possibility the low tracks closer to the NJ / 
Delmarva coast this weekend. Regardless of exact position, we are 
likely to be on the drier (subsidence) side of the system with 
northwest winds bringing in breezy, warmer, and mostly dry 
conditions. If the Nor'easter tracks closer to our area that could 
bring some rain chances to the area, especially along/east of I-95, 
along with the potential for increasing winds. Safe to say that 
there isn't a definite trend for this weekend, so be sure to keep 
track of the forecast for any changes in the coming days.

The Nor'easter is eventually pushed offshore at the start of next 
week as high pressure builds in from the OH Valley and Great Lakes. 
Mid-level ridging builds over much of the eastern CONUS during the 
middle of next week, marking the return of much warmer temperatures 
and continued dry conditions.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Improving aviation conditions are expected tonight, especially at 
terminals north of CHO. Strengthening high pressure wedging in from 
southeast Canada will yield drier air from northeast to southwest 
across the terminals. Expect VFR conditions for all terminals east 
of the Alleghenies prior 00-03z/8-11pm. A leftover shower/sprinkle 
is possible at CHO/SHD points west through the same aforementioned 
time above. Further improvements are expected overnight as low cigs 
continue to lift and mid/high level cloud cover scatters out. 
Pockets of MVFR to VFR conditions are expected across the terminals 
tonight with VFR Thursday morning into Thursday afternoon. The 
strengthening high to the north combined with developing Nor'easter 
off the coast will yield even more dry air into the region 
allowing for further improvement Thursday and Friday where VFR 
conditions prevail.

Winds will remain gusty out of the north and northeast at 20 to 30 
kts. Highest gusts will likely be during the afternoon and evening 
hours with some tapering during the evening and overnight periods. 

A strong Nor'easter off the coast near Southern New England to NJ 
will bring breezy northwest winds this weekend (gusts around 20-25 
knots possible). Some showers are possible east of BWI/MTN, but 
highly uncertain as it will depend how close the low pressure gets 
to our area. Continue to monitor for any additional impacts. Overall 
looking at VFR conditions this weekend into early next week. Winds 
will slowly taper Monday and Tuesday as low pressure finally pulls 
away. 

&&

.MARINE...
High end Small Craft Advisories remain in effect for all waters with 
Gale Warnings in effect for the surrounding waters around southern MD 
through tonight. High end Small Craft Advisories are in effect for 
all waters Thursday through Thursday night for continued gusty north 
to northeast flow. Additional SCAs are needed in gusty north to 
northeast flow Friday. 

High-end SCA conditions to Gales are possible this weekend over the 
waters, especially in the Chesapeake Bay due to the strong 
Nor'easter that will be off the coast. If the low tracks closer to 
our area, expect higher gusts over the waters. However, there 
remains a lot of uncertainty in the forecast, so be sure to check 
back as conditions become more certain through the week.


&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
A long duration coastal flood event is expected through the weekend 
within persistent onshore flow. Coastal Flood Warnings are in effect 
for St. Mary's and Annapolis through the next few high tide cycles.
 
At Alexandria, a Coastal Flood Advisory today through Thursday 
morning is followed with a high end Coastal Flood Advisory 
Thursday afternoon through Friday morning. At Dahlgren and 
Solomons Island, Coastal Flood Advisories extend through 
Thursday night.

Anomalies will be lower further north on the Bay, but we'll need to 
keep an eye on Baltimore and Havre de Grace Friday into the weekend, 
as well as DC on the Upper Tidal Potomac. Decisions will likely need 
to be made this afternoon and evening regarding whether any 
additional warnings or advisories are needed.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...Coastal Flood Advisory from 5 AM Thursday to 9 AM EDT Friday 
     for DCZ001.
MD...Small Craft Advisory until 6 AM EDT Friday for MDZ008.
     Coastal Flood Warning from 11 PM this evening to 11 AM EDT 
     Friday for MDZ014.
     Coastal Flood Advisory until 7 AM EDT Friday for MDZ016.
     Coastal Flood Warning until 5 PM EDT Friday for MDZ017.
     Coastal Flood Advisory until 8 AM EDT Friday for MDZ018.
VA...Coastal Flood Advisory until 7 AM EDT Friday for VAZ057.
     Coastal Flood Advisory until 2 PM EDT Thursday for VAZ054.
     Coastal Flood Watch from Thursday afternoon through Friday 
     morning for VAZ054.
WV...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 6 AM EDT Friday for ANZ530>532-535-
     536-538>540.
     Gale Warning until 6 AM EDT Thursday for ANZ533-534-537-
     541>543.
     Small Craft Advisory from 6 AM Thursday to 6 AM EDT Friday for 
     ANZ533-534-537-541>543.

&&

$$

alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 23 at 3:08PM EDT until September 25 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
alerts.desc:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low lying areas due to tidal flooding.

* WHERE...Shoreline in the District of Columbia.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Thursday to 9 AM EDT Friday, especially
around the time of high tide.

* IMPACTS... The unprotected area on the Southwest Waterfront at
the DC Seafood Market is expected to flood. Water is expected to
approach parts of the Hains Point Loop Road, but it will likely
be closed.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides two to two and a half feet above
normal. The next high tide at Washington Channel is at 6:49 PM
and 7:04 AM.
